Although the surge did not change, the record states the rider was not notified of the surge change at all (F9), so no notice satisfying SURGE-1 (new multiplier, revised estimated fare, free cancellation) was given; on a later corrected reading this is a notice breach, not a fare-quantity breach.

There is no route deviation to refund: actual distance 2.3 km was 0.1 km shorter than the 2.4 km optimal route, well inside the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, and trip time 3.6 min was under the 4.8 min estimate.

The driver's written statement says only that pricing is the app's and that he drove the app route; it does not deny the words the rider reports, and the chat log on file contains no pricing exchange between them.

The complaint — 'he said he knows where I live and I had better just pay', with the rider stating 'I felt unsafe for the rest of the ride' — is a threat and a safety/intimidation allegation, whatever the fare arithmetic shows; it must be screened to a human.

Both accounts are otherwise clean — rider 5.0 with 0 upheld disputes in 90 days, driver 4.58 with 0 upheld disputes — so no repeat-deviation or fraud flag is supported by the profiles, and the profiles cannot decide the fare question either way.

weaknesses: The fare facts cut against any dollar refund: F6/F7/F8 show the multiplier was 1.3x both at quote and at trip start and the metered fare ($11.81) is $0.50 below the quote ($12.31), so the driver side will argue SURGE-2 'unchanged → quoted fare applies' and no_action.

The only notice fact, F9, is internally inconsistent with F4/F6/F7 (it says a surge 'change' occurred when none did), so the driver will say it is a stale log entry and there is no proven SURGE-1 notice defect to hang a refund on.

The chat record (F12) is complete and contains no pricing conversation and no driver message about where the rider lives, so the intimidation words rest only on the rider's own complaint statement, which the system records do not corroborate — RD-5/TH-3 credibility will be contested.
F1/F3 show the rider was driven 0.1 km shorter than optimal, so any route-based grievance (RD-1 to RD-3) is unsupported and the driver will use F1–F3 to show compliance.
F15 shows a 588-day, 528-trip driver with 0 upheld disputes, which the other side will use on TH-3 credibility against the rider's uncorroborated account of the driver's words.

claims.assertion: The rider was quoted $12.31 at 1.3x surge (F6) and was actually charged $11.81 (F5), i.e. $0.50 LESS than the quote, because the surge multiplier never changed from 1.3x (F8).

No surge differential exists to refund: the multiplier at quote and at trip start was 1.3x in both records (F4, F7, F8), so SURGE-3's condition 'the whole difference comes from surge' cannot be satisfied and the differential is zero.

The no-notice fact (F9) is immaterial on these numbers: SURGE-2 refunds only the surge differential when the surge ROSE without notice, and here the surge did not rise (F8) and the charged fare undercut the quote (F5, F6).

The fare build-up is exactly the policy formula: base $3.90 + distance $3.29 (2.33 km) + time $0.93 (3.6 min) + platform/booking fee $1.25, with no waiting fee, giving $11.81 (F5), and the booking fee was not surged (F7).

There is no route element to this dispute: billed distance 2.3 km is 0.1 km SHORTER than the optimal 2.4 km (F3, F1) and the trip took 3.6 min against an estimate of 4.8 min (F2), so no deviation exists and nothing is refundable under RD-1/RD-2.
The driver's written account that he picked up on time and drove the app route (F13) is corroborated by the system records: a 2.3 km track against a 2.4 km optimum (F1) with a 3.6 min duration (F2).

Nothing in the chat record shows the driver making any demand about money: the only two timestamped messages are the rider's pickup note and the driver's car description (F10, F11, F12), and the driver's written statement explains pricing is the app's (F13).

The driver's history shows no upheld dispute of any type in 90 days (F15), so the repeat-deviation add-on and the fraud threshold in RD-6 / TH-3 are not engaged; the amount in issue is under $10 so the system decides it (TH-1).

weaknesses: F9 ('Surge log: the rider was not notified of the surge change') is on the record against us; the rider will argue that on a strict reading of SURGE-1 and SURGE-2, no notice of the in-effect multiplier was given, and an adjudicator might treat the notice failure as a ground for relief even though the surge did not change (F8).

The rider's complaint alleges the driver said 'he knows where I live' — a threat allegation with no message in the chat record (F10, F11, F12) and no driver admission (F13); if the judge reads that complaint text as an intimidation indicator, SAFE-1/SAFE-2 remove the case from the system and send it to a person, where the driver cannot rely on the fare arithmetic.
Our case rests entirely on system records (F3–F9); the driver's own denial (F13) adds nothing beyond them, so the outcome stands or falls on the fare and GPS data alone.
The driver's rating of 4.58 with 528 trips (F15) is lower than the rider's 5.0 (F14), which the rider may use on the credibility criterion in TH-3.

points.response: Conceded on the arithmetic: the multiplier was 1.3x at quote and at trip start (F4, F6, F7) and the metered total $11.81 (F5) is below the $12.31 quote (F6), so no surge overcharge exists. My case was never for the $0.50 — it is for the notice defect (F9) and the safety allegation.

Accepted: with the multiplier unchanged at 1.3x (F4, F7, F8) the surge differential is zero and SURGE-3's differential measure yields nothing to refund. That is why I did not ask for a dollar figure and instead seek escalation.

F9 says the rider was 'not notified of the surge change' — that is a system-logged notice failure, and it is unresolved on the face of the record because F4/F6/F7/F8 say no change occurred; a notice breach of SURGE-1 (new multiplier, revised fare, free cancellation) is not cured by the fare happening to land $0.50 below the quote (F5, F6), so the case cannot simply be closed as no_action on that basis.
Not contested: the build-up in F5 matches the FARE-0 formula and the booking fee was not surged (F7), so the fare arithmetic is correct — the dispute is not the arithmetic.
Conceded: actual 2.3 km against a 2.4 km optimum (F1, F3) is inside the 1 km tolerance of RD-1, so there is no route deviation and nothing is refundable under RD-1/RD-2.

The absence of the threat in the chat log (F10, F11, F12) is exactly the point: the rider's report of those words sits entirely in the filed complaint, so the record is silent rather than exculpatory, and the driver's statement (F13) addresses pricing and route only (F1, F2) — he never denies saying it, which leaves a safety screening duty under SAFE-1 rather than a finding for either side.
Agreed that no repeat-deviation or fraud add-on is engaged: both profiles show 0 upheld disputes (F14, F15), so RD-6 / TH-3 thresholds are not in play and the profiles can never decide the case.

Withdrawn as a refund ground only: my own C3 asked for no money, and the fare facts show nothing was overcharged (F5, F6, F8), so I rest the notice point solely as a reason for human review, not as a basis for a dollar award.

Conceded on the arithmetic — the rider's own figures match ours: quote $12.31 (F6), charged $11.81 (F5, F7), i.e. $0.50 under the quote — but the conclusion the rider draws is the wrong way round: since nothing was overcharged relative to FARE-0's build-up (F5) and the multiplier never moved (F8), there is no differential for SURGE-3 to compute.

Agreed and relied on: the multiplier was 1.3x at quote and 1.3x at trip start (F4, F6, F8), so SURGE-2's 'surge rose, rider not notified' row cannot be triggered and the applicable row is 'unchanged → quoted fare applies', which is $0.50 MORE than what was charged.

F9 records no notification of a surge change, but SURGE-1's notice duty attaches only where the multiplier rises before trip start and nothing on the record shows a rise (F4, F6, F8); a log line describing a 'change' that did not occur proves no defect in the delivered fare, and the charge is the quote (F6) less $0.50 (F5).
Conceded: actual 2.3 km against optimal 2.4 km (F1, F3) is inside RD-1's 1 km tolerance, so no RD-2 refund arises and no driver violation is recorded on the route.

The chat record is complete (F12) and contains no pricing exchange and no message from the driver about the rider's home (F10, F11); the driver's statement that pricing is the app's and he drove the app route (F13) is corroborated by the GPS track (F1, F2), so the reported words rest only on the rider's uncorroborated complaint.

Agreed, and it cuts against escalation: neither profile carries a fraud flag or an upheld dispute (F14, F15), the amount in issue is under $10 and the records are complete, so TH-1/TH-2 make the system ruling final rather than sending a $0.50-under-quote fare to a human.

The rider's request for escalation has no clause hook on this record: there is no off-route segment to exempt or refund (F1, F3) and no missing record — messages are timestamped and complete (F12) — so TH-4 (missing records) and RD-5 (escalate on a no-road-name agreement) are not engaged.
